articles.title: TCS Pune Facility Launches India's First Lights-Out Factory Lab - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News TCS Opens Pune’s First Lights-Out Factory Lab for AI Manufacturing Breaking News TCS Opens Pune’s First Lights-Out Factory Lab for AI Manufacturing By Urban Acres September 9, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp PUNE | September 9, 2026 — TCS has launched an Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab at its Sahyadri Park campus in Pune, describing the facility as India’s first lights-out factory lab aimed at advancing artificial intelligence-led manufacturing. The announcement was made by Tata Consultancy Services on Wednesday through a regulatory filing. The facility includes a fully robotic battery pack assembly line designed to demonstrate how autonomous systems can operate a manufacturing process with minimal human intervention. A lights-out factory is a manufacturing facility in which autonomous systems run production lines with limited human involvement. TCS said its new Pune lab will allow manufacturers to prototype, validate and scale AI-first production systems in a live, multi-stage setup while reducing the risks associated with deployment. The facility combines digital twins, robotics, industrial artificial intelligence, factory control systems and real-time operational intelligence. TCS said the setup simulates how self-optimising factories can automate workflows and coordinate production activities. “ With our state-of-the-art TCS Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab Lights-Out Factory, we are advancing TCS’ vision of engineering AI-first production systems,” Sreenivasa Chakravarti, Global Head and Vice President of Industrial Autonomy and Engineering at TCS, said in the company’s statement. “We have built a facility that can help customers turn their aspiration of lights-out manufacturing into a reality.” Chakravarti said the lab would demonstrate how a “Human + AI” model could help enterprises move from digitally enabled operations towards increasingly autonomous production systems. The statement did not disclose the investment in the facility, its employee strength or the number of manufacturers expected to use the lab. The Pune facility will support industrial applications including predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection, real-time process optimisation, human-machine collaboration and autonomous factory operations. These use cases cover both the monitoring of industrial equipment and the automation of production-related decisions. The launch adds an industrial automation facility to Pune’s technology and engineering ecosystem, although TCS did not specify whether the lab would support a particular manufacturing sector beyond the battery pack assembly demonstration. The company also did not announce a public commissioning date for customer projects or provide an implementation timeline for moving systems tested at the lab into operating factories. TCS’s next stated step is to use the facility to help manufacturers prototype, validate and scale AI-first production systems across the listed industrial use cases. articles.title: TCS launches ' India's first ' lights-out factory lab to accelerate AI -led manufacturing
articles.content: Hi-Tech 2 min read TCS launches ‘India's first’ lights-out factory lab to accelerate AI-led manufacturing The Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab – Lights-Out Factory combines digital twins, industrial AI, robotics, factory control systems and real-time operational intelligence to demonstrate how manufacturing operations can function with minimal human intervention. ETManufacturing Desk ETManufacturing Published On Sep 9, 2026 at 04:40 PM IST Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook The facility will allow companies to move beyond isolated automation projects and explore integrated approaches spanning engineering, manufacturing and factory operations. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) on Wednesday launched what it claims is India's first lights-out factory lab , a facility designed to help manufacturers simulate and validate AI-driven autonomous production systems before deploying them on the shop floor. The Pune-based facility features a fully robotic battery pack assembly line and will enable manufacturers to test AI, digital twins , robotics and autonomous production systems before deployment. Advt Located at TCS' Sahyadri Park campus in Pune, the Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab – Lights-Out Factory combines digital twins, industrial AI, robotics, factory control systems and real-time operational intelligence to demonstrate how manufacturing operations can function with minimal human intervention. The company said the facility houses a fully robotic battery pack assembly line, making it the first lab in India to demonstrate lights-out manufacturing principles through a live production environment. Manufacturers will be able to use the setup to prototype, validate and scale AI-first production systems across multiple stages of manufacturing. A lights-out factory refers to a manufacturing facility where autonomous systems can operate production processes with little or no human presence. TCS said the new lab addresses a major challenge faced by industrial companies translating Industry 4.0, artificial intelligence and robotics initiatives into practical operating models while reducing deployment risks. The launch comes as manufacturers increasingly seek to improve operational efficiency, resilience and agility amid growing production complexities. According to the company’s statement, the facility will allow companies to move beyond isolated automation projects and explore integrated approaches spanning engineering, manufacturing and factory operations. Advt The lab will support a range of use cases including predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection, real-time process optimisation, human-machine collaboration and autonomous factory operations. "The lab provides a tangible demonstration of how the Human + AI model can help enterprises progress from digitally enabled operations to increasingly autonomous production systems," said Sreenivasa Chakravarti, Global Head and Vice President, Industrial Autonomy and Engineering, TCS. articles.title: GRSE Launches Sagar Manthan, India's First Indigenous Ocean Research Vessel for Deep ...
articles.content: Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) Ltd, a Navratna Defence Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, launched Sagar Manthan, the Ocean Research Vessel (ORV) for the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, on Wednesday. This is the first ORV of its kind to be built in India. The launch comes barely five months after the keel laying of the vessel, highlighting the shipyard's capability to maintain schedules. Dr Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Science and Technology and Ministry of Earth Sciences, who was supposed to attend the event as chief guest virtually, was unable to do so. He, however, sent a message congratulating both GRSE and NCPOR for the achievement. The Minister also highlighted the important role that the ORV will play in India's deep ocean research once it is delivered in 2028. Dr Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, was present as the guest of honour at the event at GRSE’s Rishi Bankim Shipyard in Kolkata. In his address, the secretary, who is a renowned oceanographer, spoke on the importance of ocean research for the country's development. "We are also building a Marine Acoustic Research Vessel (ARV) for the Ministry of Defence and two Coastal Research Vessels (CRVs). Till now, we used to say that GRSE has achieved Atmanirbharta in warship building. From now onwards, we can say that GRSE has achieved Atmanirbharta, both in the field of warships and specialised vessels," Cmde P R Hari, IN (Retd), chairman and managing director, GRSE, said. The 89.50 m long, 18.80 m wide ORV will have a gross tonnage of 5,900 tonnes and its speed will be 14 knots at 90 per cent maximum continuous rating (MCR). Once delivered, the ORV will be capable of Underway Swath Multibeam as well as Geophysical Seismic surveys in coastal seas and deep waters at a maximum depth of 6 km. She will also be able to carry out Conductivity, Temperature and Depth (CTD) profiling and water sampling operations such as biological sampling using vertical and horizontal methods through various nets. The research vessel will also effectively carry out surface and deep-sea mooring and data buoy operations, seabed sampling using corers and grabs as well as rock dredging with chain bag dredges. The vessel will also undertake underway atmospheric observations, surface meteorological and current measurements, and collect upper air data. Scientists will be able to carry out analytical work and data processing on board. The ship will also provide training and education to scientists and technicians. GRSE has the necessary expertise in the field of survey vessels and has been building them for the Indian Navy for nearly four decades now. The shipyard delivered survey ships to the Navy in the 80s. It also built and delivered the Marine Acoustic Research Vessel INS Sagardhwani to the Naval Physical and Oceanographic Laboratory (NPOL) in 1994. The ship is still in service and recently underwent a refit...

articles.title: India's First AI Acoustic System Boosts Forest, Wildlife Conservation - Rediff.com
articles.content: Discover how the Haldwani forest division is pioneering India's first AI-based forest acoustic surveillance system, revolutionising real-time detection of illegal activities and significantly boosting wildlife conservation efforts. In a landmark technological breakthrough for forest conservation, the Haldwani forest division has successfully demonstrated India's first Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based forest acoustic surveillance system, capable of detecting illegal logging and wildlife crime among others, a senior official said on Wednesday. Designed specifically for local forest conditions, the system integrates AI, edge computing, acoustic sensors and long-range wireless communication to continuously monitor forest sounds and instantly identify suspicious activities, even in remote areas where conventional mobile networks are unavailable, he said. The system is powered by solar energy with rechargeable batteries, enabling uninterrupted round-the-clock operation even in remote forest areas without access to the electricity grid, said Kundan Kumar, Divisional Forest Officer (DFO), Haldwani forest division. Unlike traditional surveillance systems that depend largely on manual patrolling and periodic inspections, the forest acoustic surveillance system functions as an intelligent "digital ear" inside the forest, he said. The AI-powered acoustic sensors continuously analyse sounds generated within the forest ecosystem and automatically recognise events of security and ecological importance, Kumar said. "The AI-based surveillance system is an innovative indigenous technology that showcases a new era in forest protection, anti-poaching and wildlife conservation, "he told PTI. The system has already been trained to detect chainsaw operation, axe chopping, gunshots, vehicle movement, human intrusion, wildlife vocalisations and other suspicious anthropogenic activities, said Kumar, a 2017-batch Indian Forest Service (IFoS) officer. Whenever such events are detected, the AI analyses the sound locally on edge devices and instantly transmits an alert through the LoRa (long range) communication network to the forest control room, enabling rapid deployment of field staff and significantly reducing response time, he said. The technology is expected to transform forest protection by providing an effective early warning mechanism against illegal logging, timber smuggling, poaching and wildlife crime, the official said. The ability to detect suspicious activities in real time will considerably strengthen surveillance in vulnerable forest areas, protected areas and wildlife habitats while enhancing the operational efficiency and safety of frontline forest personnel. Beyond enforcement, the platform represents a major advancement in wildlife conservation and biodiversity monitoring, he said. The AI system can automatically recognise the vocalisations of different wildlife species, enabling continuous monitoring of wildlife presence, movement and habitat use. The data generated by the system will support biodiversity assessment, ecological research, habitat management and long-term conservation planning, Kumar said. The modular architecture of the platform allows future integration with camera traps, drones, Geographic Information System (GIS)-based monitoring systems, forest fire early warning systems and central command-and-control centres, creating a comprehensive Smart Forest Surveillance Network capable of protecting forests through intelligent technologies, he added. Developed as an indigenous solution tailored for Uttarakhand forests, this innovation demonstrates the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence in environmental governance. It combines conservation science with cutting-edge technology to address some of the most pressing challenges facing forests today", Kumar said. The initiative...

articles.title: PM Narendra Modi Witnesses Perfios' Showcase of the AI -Powered Future of Banking at GFF 2026
articles.content: In a major milestone for India’s financial technology sector at the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, Perfios, India’s leading B2B SaaS TechFin, was selected among an elite cohort of six technology companies to present its AI breakthroughs for BFSI directly to Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The high-profile showcase highlighted Perfios’ role as the technological backbone of India’s evolving financial ecosystem. Perfios unveiled its next-generation Agentic AI Operating system – a smart, autonomous operating system designed to help banks evaluate credit based on everyday real-world data, making formal loans accessible to millions of underserved citizens across India. Moving beyond traditional software wrappers, Perfios demonstrated how its AI agents operate as autonomous, self-learning entities built on Perfios’ two decades of experience in the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) sector. With 90% of India’s digital loans powered by Perfios, 1,000+ Banks, NBFCs and fintechs relying on its technology, and its solutions powering financial institutions across 20+ countries, Perfios is helping enable faster and fairer access to credit for 25M+ businesses. “Presenting our vision directly to Prime Minister Narendra Modi was an extraordinary honour for all of us at Perfios,” said Nitin Chugh, Managing Director and Group CEO, Perfios. “During the showcase, we demonstrated how Agentic AI can drive meaningful change across rural communities, MSMEs and Young India. For instance, a rural woman cattle grazer seeking credit could be assessed using everyday signals such as dairy collection payouts, milk yield history and UPI transactions to build a credible credit profile and unlock formal credit. From helping small shop owners access government schemes to guiding young adults with smart budgeting, our AI agents are making financial services simpler, faster and fairer for everyone.” During the live interaction with PM Modi, Perfios highlighted how its AI technology transforms lives across three key pillars of India’s economy: For Rural India: Turns daily dairy collection payouts and UPI records into a trusted credit profile, giving rural farmers direct access to formal bank loans. For Small Businesses (MSMEs): Combines GST, trade, and banking data in seconds to help small business owners quickly find and apply for government funding schemes like PM Mudra (PMMY) and PM Vishwakarma. For Young India: Analyzes earning, saving, and spending habits to offer personalized budgeting advice and timely investment guidance. The interaction with the Prime Minister showcased India’s Agentic AI growth story and the role of homegrown innovation in shaping the future of financial services. At GFF 2026, from September 9 to 11, Perfios will showcase ‘Agents You Can Bank On’, its portfolio of eight specialized AI solutions spanning the financial services ecosystem, at Booth i1. Lending featured CAM, Agentic Underwriting and Data Intelligence Bridge (DIB), supporting automated credit assessment, AI-assisted underwriting and intelligent document processing and orchestration. Fraud and Compliance featured Clari5 Genie and DPDP Suite, enabling AI-led fraud and AML investigations and supporting organisations in operationalising compliance with India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Insurance featured Agentic Distribution and Health Claims and Agentic PAS, applying AI across onboarding, distribution, underwriting, claims...

articles.title: India's First Indigenously Manufactured Bullet Train to Undergo Testing by May or June 2027
articles.content: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that India's first indigenously manufactured bullet train is expected to begin testing on railway tracks by May or June 2027 at the 'NaMo for Viksit Bharat' event in Vadodara. He said the train's first body frame has already been completed and sent for a squeeze test, which is an important step in checking its strength and safety. According to the minister, the train will undergo testing for around two to four months after it reaches the tracks. The Prime Minister will inaugurate it after successful trials, and it is planned to cover the distance between Vadodara and Mumbai in about 90 minutes once the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor becomes operational. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor is 508 km long and passes through Gujarat, Maharashtra and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. The Surat-Bilimora section is expected to become operational first, with services targeted for 2027. Construction of the Vapi-Surat section is expected to be completed by December 2026. The complete corridor will have 12 stations: Mumbai (BKC), Thane, Virar, Boisar, Vapi, Bilimora, Surat, Bharuch, Vadodara, Anand, Ahmedabad and Sabarmati. The indigenous bullet train is part of the government's Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, which aims to increase domestic manufacturing and reduce dependence on foreign technology, representing an important step in India's development of high-speed rail technology. The minister also highlighted wider railway development, saying that 280 railway stations have been redeveloped and 36,000 km of new railway tracks have been developed. He said these improvements, along with projects such as the Chenab Bridge and the railway connection to Mizoram, show the changing face of Indian Railways. articles.title: POVA Expands AI Ecosystem with Smart Features Across Its Latest Devices
articles.content: POVA is taking this shift a step further by building an AI ecosystem that goes beyond the smartphone, bringing practical intelligence across its latest devices to make everyday tasks simpler. The POVA 8 Series, including the POVA 8 and POVA 8 Pro, forms the foundation of this ecosystem. The POVA 8 Pro 5G comes with an India’s first AI Assistant designed to make everyday tasks more convenient, from managing information to helping users get things done with fewer steps. It can record, transcribe and summarise regular and WhatsApp calls in English, Hindi, Bengali and Marathi, helping users keep track of important conversations without having to make notes manually. Its Alive Matrix Display also puts notifications, battery status and timers at a glance, while doubling up as a desk clock when the phone is placed face down. Adding to this is the POVA AI Buds Pro, designed to bring AI into meetings, classes and everyday conversations. With a single press on the charging case, users can start recording and later access transcripts, summaries and action items. The earbuds also support real-time translation across 12 Indian languages, making conversations easier across different language preferences. Together, the POVA 8 Series and AI Buds Pro reflect POVA’s approach to building an ecosystem where each device has a practical role. Instead of adding AI simply for the sake of it, POVA is using it to take care of everyday tasks in the background, helping users save time and stay focused on what they are doing. With its latest products now launched in India, POVA is building towards a connected AI experience where the smartphone and companion devices work together to make everyday technology more useful. articles.title: Wondrlab Launches WondrAgents, India's First Unified Agentic Operating System for End-to ...
articles.content: PRNewswire Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], September 8: Wondrlab today unveiled WondrAgents, India's first unified Agentic Operating System for influencer marketing, powering its influencer marketing platforms OPA and Opportune. Built as a network of seven specialised AI agents, WondrAgents seamlessly executes the complete influencer campaign lifecycle, from campaign brief and creator discovery to outreach, negotiation, contracting, content evaluation and ROI reporting, helping brands reduce campaign go-live time by up to 70% while delivering measurable business outcomes. The launch marks the next evolution of Wondrlab's 'Total Influence' vision, bringing together years of influencer marketing expertise, proprietary creator intelligence, campaign learnings and machine learning into a unified operating system that enables brands to execute influencer campaigns with greater speed, transparency and precision. Unlike conventional AI tools that automate individual tasks, WondrAgents is designed as a unified 'Agentic Operating System' where seven specialised AI agents work alongside campaign teams to power every stage of campaign execution. Each agent is trained to optimise against a brand's campaign objectives, from campaign planning and creator discovery to negotiation, content evaluation and performance reporting, while human teams continue to lead strategy, creativity and relationship management. The launch addresses one of the industry's biggest challenges, where brands continue to rely on disconnected tools, manual coordination and fragmented reporting. By bringing the entire influencer marketing workflow onto a single unified intelligent operating system across OPA and Opportune, our SaaS platforms, WondrAgents enables greater operational efficiency, complete campaign visibility and continuous optimisation throughout the campaign lifecycle. Speaking about the launch, Vandana Verma, Co-Founder, Wondrlab Network, said, "Since 2020, we've built one of India's largest influencer marketing ecosystems through OPA and Opportune. Every campaign we've executed has added to the rich knowledge base of creator intelligence, brand insights and campaign learnings. WondrAgents is built on that proprietary knowledge base. We've invested significantly in training these agents with years of experience, and we will continue investing in agentic AI because we believe the future of influencer marketing lies in humans and AI agents working together to deliver faster execution, smarter decisions and better outcomes for brands." Shidush Contractor, Chief Operating Officer, OPA & Opportune, added, "We're excited to introduce India's first unified Agentic Operating System for influencer marketing. WondrAgents is built to tackle the toughest campaign briefs, bringing together great minds, specialised AI agents and years of campaign intelligence to execute faster and smarter. From evaluating creators and generating personalised scripts to optimising campaign performance, the platform takes care of the operational complexity, allowing teams to focus on ideas, creativity and strategic decisions. This isn't about replacing people; it's about combining human intelligence with AI agents to deliver greater transparency, measurable impact and a new level of efficiency for brands." Today, every influencer campaign starts almost from scratch, with campaign knowledge scattered across multiple tools, platforms and teams. WondrAgents change that by building a living intelligence library for every brand. articles.title: Two mission control centres for Gaganyaan set up - The New Indian Express
articles.content: BENGALURU: India’s first manned space mission, the Gaganyaan mission, will have two mission control centre, which the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has set up in Bengaluru and Sriharikota, and which will handle primary and secondary mission for its uncrewed mission scheduled to be late this year as well as the crewed mission slated to be launched in the first quarter of 2027. Speaking on the second day of the three-day 9th edition of Bengaluru Space Expo- 2026 in Bengaluru, SS Vinod, Gaganyaan project director, said that while the international mission control centres will be used for communication in the Gaganyaan crewed and uncrewed missions, the primary control and data operations will be from India and this was a major step towards the missions, for which the two mission control centres at Bengaluru and Sriharikota will be used. He said that as ISRO Chairman V Narayanan recently announced that the first uncrewed mission (Gaganyaan-1, or G-1) would be carried out in this calendar year, it is important for many thermal and micro-gravity experiments to be carried out during this mission. For the main Gaganyaan mission – the human mission, or the crewed mission – apart from laying importance on the technological aspects, work also continues on improving the psychological and physiological aspects of the crew. He said this sector needed to be improved upon, while technology should be focused on. Biju SR, Director, Human Space Flight Centre, ISRO, said that for the immediate Gaganyaan mission the Launch Vehicle Mark-III (LVM3) – which was previously known as the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark-III (GSLV Mk-III) – will be used, and work on imparting world-class training to the astronauts from a dedicated centre in Bengaluru is ongoing. ‘ 3RD PARTY INSURANCE FOR SATS LAUNCHED BY PVT COS’ Bengaluru: Prafulla Kumar Jain, director, Programme Management and Authorisation Directorate, Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), said the government is working on launching third party insurance scheme for satellites launched by private companies. The government had already approved this insurance for launch operations. Discussions for the satellites and the liability period are under discussion. IN-SPACe already provides launch support and manufacturing support of 50% and 30%, respectively, for Indian start-up companies, and the insurance scheme services is a new domain which the government is now looking at. To provide further support to the Indian space sector, the government also announced to extend the GST exemption to the private sector, which was so far reserved for ISRO and NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), the Commercial arm of ISRO. The government is also thinking of handing over some of the sat-buses (core structural and functional frameworks of satellites) of ISRO to the private sector for operation and maintenance and to bring in a third party review mechanism by experts to strengthen the insurance schemes. articles.content: Industry Watch Articles News Events Sports Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Kérastase India brought together over 100 women creators, influencers, padel enthusiasts and athletes for Padel in Gloss, a women-only padel platform that brought sport, beauty and lifestyle together. Built around the thought “Gloss On, Game On,” the experience celebrated women embracing movement, self-expression and new challenges. Participants included first-time players, experienced padel enthusiasts and professional athletes. The event featured personalities from entertainment, beauty, fashion and lifestyle, including singer-songwriter Lisa Mishra, actor-creator Sara Sarosh and actor Aditi Bhatia. Professional padel players, including Sakshi Malik, also joined the event, adding a competitive element to the experience. Across the day, participants took to the court while friends and fellow guests cheered from the sidelines. The experience aimed to showcase padel as both an active sport and a social lifestyle activity. Kérastase Gloss Absolu was also an integral part of the experience. The Kérastase hair station allowed guests to explore the range, experience the products first-hand and discover match-day hairstyles. Personalised Gloss Absolu bottles added a bespoke touch, while a café cart gave guests a space to connect and unwind between matches. Anjali Pai, General Manager, Kérastase India said, “Padel in Gloss celebrated the confidence great hair can unlock, giving women the freedom to express themselves and take on new challenges. It was wonderful to see the women give the game their all, feel great in their hair and make the platform their own.” With Padel in Gloss, Kérastase India brought its Gloss On, Game On vision to life, creating a space where women could play, compete, connect and express themselves while bringing beauty and an active lifestyle together.
